title: HomeFlood Loss Settlement and Claim Payment Rule
content:
**Governing report.** Each coverage on a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies claim is settled from the latest governing adjuster report.

**Dwelling.**
- The dwelling loss is taken at replacement cost when both of these hold: the tier makes dwelling replacement cost available, and the dwelling limit is at least the tier's insurance-to-value share of the dwelling replacement cost value. Otherwise it is taken at actual cash value.
- The part of the basement loss above the tier's finished basement sublimit is removed from the dwelling loss.

**Other structures.** Other structures are paid at replacement cost, up to the tier's other-structures percent of the dwelling limit.

**Personal property.** Personal property is taken on the tier's personal property settlement basis.

**Pool.** The pool loss is paid up to the tier's pool repair sublimit.

**Deductible.** One per-occurrence deductible applies once to the whole claim. It is taken in this order of coverages:
1. dwelling;
2. any remainder from other structures;
3. then personal property;
4. then the pool.

**Limits.** Each coverage is then capped at its limit.

**Loss of use and loss avoidance.** Loss of use is paid as incurred, up to the tier's loss-of-use limit, for no longer than the tier's loss-of-use period after the date of loss. Loss-avoidance costs are paid up to the tier's loss-avoidance limit. Neither bears the deductible.

**Payments.** A new payment on a coverage is its payable amount less what has already been paid, net of voids, on that claim and coverage. It is issued only when positive.
- Dwelling and other-structures payments name the mortgagee of record with the insured.
- The other payments go to the insured alone.

**Voids.** A void reverses one issued payment item in full, by its reference, and the amount is reissued under a new reference.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical inputs)

The policy is HomeFlood Plus: dwelling limit 400,000 USD, dwelling replacement cost value 450,000 USD, deductible 5,000 USD.
- Insurance-to-value: 80 percent of 450,000 is 360,000. The dwelling limit reaches it, so the dwelling loss is taken at replacement cost.
- Basement: the report shows a dwelling replacement cost loss of 30,000 USD, of which 28,000 USD is in a finished basement. The basement part above the 25,000 USD Plus sublimit (3,000 USD) is removed, leaving 27,000 USD.
- Deductible: the whole 5,000 USD is taken from the dwelling, leaving 22,000 USD payable on the dwelling and nothing of the deductible for the other coverages.
